g.text: CONFIG HOT-RELOAD PROPAGATION (agent/config_reload.py)
Save Applies Immediately -- No Restart Required, Except Three Process-Startup-Bound BE Settings
1. POST /api/config -- config_schema.save_values(request.values)
Writes ONLY changed keys to agent/.env and/or BE/.env. An empty value REMOVES that key's line (falls back to code default) instead of writing KEY="".
2. If agent keys changed: config_reload.reload_all()
load_dotenv(agent/.env, override=True) -- authoritative over whatever this process already loaded --
then importlib.reload(agent_config), importlib.reload(log_config): re-executes both modules IN PLACE (same object identity).
If BE keys changed: get_settings.cache_clear() -- every BE module already reads via a fresh get_settings() call, so this alone is the whole fix.
3. Push into every consumer that copied a value by name
`from agent_config import X` COPIES the value at import time --
reassigning agent_config.X later never reaches that copy.
setattr() on each already-imported module (sys.modules lookup,
never a fresh import -- avoids circular-import ordering):
shared, shell_tools (aliased names), confirm,
auto_runner, fs_tools, memory
Derived values recomputed from their source, not read
from agent_config directly: fs_tools.BASE_DIR = WORKSPACE_DIR.resolve(),
shell_tools.BASE_DIR, memory.MEMORY_PATH = Path(MEMORY_FILE)
4. Same idea, one hop further: BE-side modules
app.api.memory (MEMORY_FILE), app.core.approval_bridge
(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), app.core.agent_bridge AND
app.api.chat -- chat.py copied agent_bridge's OWN copy of
CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT again at ITS import time; missing this one
meant Save updated the schema's answer but not what "New chat"
actually seeded _messages with.
OllamaAgent.model is an instance attribute set once at
construction, not a module-level name -- a model change instead
drops agent_bridge's cached singleton so the next chat request
builds a fresh one.
Exception: BE_HOST / BE_PORT / BE_CORS_ORIGINS still need a real restart
Bound to the process at startup -- the socket is already listening and CORS middleware already installed into the ASGI app by the time Save runs.
UNLIMITED_MODE -- same reload mechanism, one setting, many call sites
Checked directly as a global at each site (not via that cap's own value), so flipping it always means "wait/run as long as it takes":
shared.py -- run_agent()'s wall-clock check skipped; round loop uses itertools.count() instead of range(max_iterations)
(checked as a body-level global on purpose -- max_iterations is a default-argument value, frozen at def time, so a reload can't change it retroactively)
_effective_tool_timeout() returns None; CHAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS / CHAT_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS waits become unbounded
shell_tools.py -- run_command's subprocess timeout removed
confirm.py -- confirm() forces timeout_seconds=None regardless of the default or any explicit caller value
auto_runner.py -- auto-mode's max_tool_calls becomes None (run_agent's own "no extra cap" sentinel)
Deliberately does NOT touch MAX_REPEAT_CALLS (stuck-loop detection) -- a malfunction, never legitimate work.
